findings.reason: the plan must either scope the sweep (the actual cost) or state the occupied-window allowance under which the second pass is taken, else the coordinator measures a gate §15 cannot produce and opens a section for a cost §15 never removed.
findings.text: §15's Why measures the 6.5 s and 11.3 s reads entirely inside `_reuse_covered` → `covered_dir_identity` → `_dir_identity`, but the deliverable only keeps `_CACHE` alive across uncovered changes and leaves that per-directory stat sweep untouched, so the first read after any covered HTML/figure change pays the sweep again — about 2,500 `stat` calls (`reckon/metadata_index.py:435`, which stats every recorded directory on every cold read) — and §15's acceptance ("the coordinator repeats §7's live passes … The second pass must answer in under 1 s") is measured on `/_index/reckon` over a 60 s live window in which a plan or evidence file is edited continuously (this plan itself was edited the same hour), so the clause is a coin-flavoured live measurement rather than something the section's mechanism delivers

findings.reason: the missing capability sits in the same module the deliverable already edits, and case (1)'s control ("drop the index on every burst") reddens if a worker takes the reader as already carrying names, so the section's own gate redirects the node without a plan change.
findings.text: §15(a) says the kernel watch's reader "keeps the names its settled burst carried", but the reader §15 names, `_FleetChangeWatch._run` (`reckon/change_streams.py:517`), obtains only a boolean from `watch.consume()` (`change_streams.py:69`) and then calls `watch.drain()`, which reads and discards the inotify bytes; no names survive to `_run` today, so the mechanism reads as already-true on a code path where it is not
